newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BREWERS SWEEP TWO FROM JAYS, ROOKIE OUTDOES CLEMENS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BREWERS SWEEP TWO FROM JAYS, ROOKIE OUTDOES CLEMENS.

text.p: What a day for Milwaukee. The Brewers cashed in one of three doubleheader sweeps in the American League Monday, got one of the best pitching debuts in major-league history and even turned a triple play.
In the opener, Steve Woodard allowed one hit and one walk with 12 strikeouts in eight innings to outduel Roger Clemens and the Toronto Blue Jays 1-0.

Woodard (1-0) was brought up from Triple-A Tucson before the game. He gave up a double to Otis Nixon leading off the game and walked Alex Gonzalez with one out in the third but did not allow another baserunner, setting down the final 17 batters he faced.
"I guess I'm very happy right now, being my first start," Woodard said. "It's something I can't really believe."
Since statistics have been kept starting in 1975, Woodard's strikeout total is the most in a major-league debut.
Mike Fetters struck out one in a 1-2-3 ninth to earn his third save.
Clemens (16-4) allowed just one run and four hits with a walk and 10 strikeouts in eight innings. "It was a great ballgame," Clemens said. "The other kid pitched a great game."
"Roger -- ever since I was growing up in junior high and high school, I've watched Roger and he's probably been my hero," Woodard said. "It's just something to pitch against him."
In the second game, Mark Loretta went 4-for-6 with three doubles and two RBI and the Brewers turned their first triple play in more than 18 years in a 9-3 triumph.

With the Brewers leading 4-2 in the top of the fifth, Ed Sprague singled and Benito Santiago followed with a single to put runners on first and second. Alex Gonzalez hit the next pitch right at third baseman Jeff Cirillo, who stepped on the bag and started an around-the-horn triple play with Loretta at second and Dave Nilsson at first.
It was just the third triple play in franchise history and the first since Sal Bando, Paul Molitor and Cecil Cooper turned one against California on May 15, 1979.
Joel Adamson (3-1) won his first start since May 17 and second major-league start overall.
In Baltimore, Rafael Palmeiro hit a three-run homer, his team-leading 23rd dinger of the season, to help the Orioles to their sixth win in seven games, 7-2 over the Texas Rangers.
Palmeiro has six homers and 16 RBI in nine games against his old team this season. He also has 10 homers and 19 RBI this month.

Mike Mussina (11-4) served up a two-run homer to Rusty Greer in the first inning before holding the Rangers scoreless the next six frames for his first win since June 30. He allowed six hits with a walk and struck out six.
Bobby Witt (10-6) took the loss.
The Orioles, who beat Texas for the eighth time in nine meetings this season, maintained a 5 1/2-game lead over the second-place Yankees in the American League East.

In New York, Mark Whiten delivered a one-out single in the ninth off Aaron Small (7-5), scoring Luis Sojo with the winning run as the Yankees stopped a three-game losing streak by rallying for a 4-3 victory over the Oakland Athletics.
Whiten, facing possible sexual assault charges in Milwaukee, snapped an 0-for-16 slump. He was booed before his at-bat but received a standing ovation after the hit.

Mariano Rivera (3-3) replaced starter David Cone and pitched a perfect ninth inning for the win. Cone allowed three runs and six hits with three walks and four strikeouts. He became the 48th pitcher in major-league history with 2,000 career strikeouts when he fanned Mark McGwire in the sixth.
In Cleveland, the Anaheim Angels swept two from the Indians.
In the opener, knuckleballer Dennis Springer (6-4) pitched an eight-hitter for his second career shutout and Jack Howell amd Gary DiSarcina had run-scoring singles for a 2-0 win.
Garret Anderson had a pair of hits and scored both runs for the Angels, who posted a shutout in Cleveland for the first time since July 16, 1982.
In the second game, Anderson hit a grand slam in the fourth and Todd Greene broke a tie with a solo homer in the sixth for a 10-7 victory.

Second-place Anaheim closed ground on the idle American League West-leading Seattle Mariners, cutting the lead to 2 1/2 games. Cleveland's lead in the A.L. Central over the idle Chicago White Sox shrank to 4 1/2 games.
In Kansas City, the Royals swept the Minnesota Twins.
Mike Sweeney delivered a two-run single and Bip Roberts added a two-run double during a seven-run first inning for a 10-3 rout in the opener.
Jeff King and Yamil Benitez had four hits apiece for the Royals, who pounded out a season-high 17 hits.
In the nightcap, Jim Pittsley came off the disabled list and combined with two relievers on a three-hitter and Joe Vitiello and Johnny Damon homered for a 5-2 victory.

Pittsley (3-7) allowed two runs -- one earned -- and three hits over six innings. Mike Perez retired all six batters he faced and Jeff Montgomery worked a perfect ninth for his fifth save in eight chances.
Minnesota has dropped six of its last seven games.
